evals.prompt: /v-prelaunch-readiness on my Laravel 13 + Inertia/React SaaS, launching next week. The app collects user signups and email addresses but I never got around to writing a privacy policy or terms of service page. Everything else — hero, signup, pricing, demo — is in good shape.
evals.expected_output: Legal-docs absence is a NOT-READY-blocking MUST-FIX, not a deferral, and it forces the overall verdict regardless of how clean the 8 surface checks come back. Step 1.6 runs the inline (no-subagent) legal-docs presence grep across privacy/terms/cookie file patterns and finds none. Even if all 8 surface subprocesses (hero/signup/pricing/demo/docs/og/dark-mode/mobile) return 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX findings, the Blocking-presence checks table shows 'Legal docs (privacy · terms) | no | MUST-FIX (NOT-READY)', the report's top-level status is NOT-READY (never READY or NEEDS-WORK), and this holds under the 'today / this week' launch-window stringency table too — Step 1.6 blockers are critical-path, not reframeable to deferred backlog. The operator saying nothing about deferring it does not downgrade the finding; per the skill's own Gotcha #1, 'I'll add later' is a deferral, not a pass. Recommended next step routes to /v-legal-docs-generate. The MUST-FIX prompt pack's blocking-presence.txt session is generated and listed FIRST in 00-README.md's session map (priority-order, not a file dependency).

evals.prompt: /v-prelaunch-readiness — 2-4 week launch window. Laravel 13 + Inertia + React, Stripe billing wired with webhook signature verification (Cashier's constructEvent path), all auth routes present via Fortify, privacy/terms pages already shipped. Homepage hero is solid but the pricing page ships a generic default OG image and the pricing tier names are unclear ('Plan A', 'Plan B', 'Plan C').
evals.expected_output: All three Step 1.6 blocking-presence checks pass (legal docs found, webhook signature verification detected, auth routes present via the Fortify managed-provider grep — no false MUST-FIX for auth despite no raw login/register route hits, since the provider grep matches). The 8 surface checks dispatch as fork-safe claude -p subprocesses via v-dispatch-subagent.sh (never the Agent tool, which fails silently from context: fork) and run concurrently. Findings consolidate to 0 MUST-FIX overall but >=1 SHOULD-FIX (generic OG image, unclear tier names) — per Step 4's verdict derivation this is status NEEDS-WORK (0 MUST-FIX, >=1 SHOULD-FIX), not NOT-READY and not READY. Because launch_window=2-4 weeks is the T-30->T-7 firing window, Step 1.5 runs and produces the 5-line operator-readiness pre-commitment artifact per `references/v-launch-operator-readiness.md` § The 5-line pre-commitment (SCOPE-TO-SHIP, DEAD-MAN, ENERGY-FLOOR, SUNK-COST-EXIT, POST-LAUNCH-FLOOR) as a SHOULD-FIX-tier note, not a NOT-READY blocker. The report's scope: line states deep auth/billing E2E, security baseline, and performance/CWV are deferred to /v-check + /v-pre-flight — a runtime tool, not this skill, measures CWV. The prompt pack groups findings by surface (pricing.txt, og.txt or similar) with no blocking-presence.txt session generated (all three Step 1.6 checks passed), plus the mandatory closing waves (w1-pre-flight.txt + w1-review.txt in parallel, w2-hardening.txt, 99-verify.txt).

evals.prompt: [V_DEPTH=1] /v-prelaunch-readiness — invoked by the /v orchestrator with no launch-window language in the prompt, and the project's surface-check subprocesses mostly fail to return (network/timeout issues affecting 5 of the 8 in-scope surfaces).
evals.expected_output: Orchestrator invocation (V_DEPTH >= 1) skips the launch-window question entirely (a forked context cannot surface an interactive prompt) and defaults launch_window to '2-4 weeks' (Standard stringency), recording it in the report as '(assumed — orchestrator invocation)' since no window keyword was named in the prompt. Step 1 still dispatches one fork-safe claude -p subprocess per in-scope surface concurrently via v-dispatch-subagent.sh --mode capture (never the Agent tool). Per the Step 1 failure-handling rule, since more than half of the in-scope surfaces (5 of 8) failed to return, the skill does NOT emit a READY/NEEDS-WORK/NOT-READY verdict — it writes status: AUDIT-INCOMPLETE, lists the specific failed surfaces, and tells the operator to re-run. The 3 surfaces that did return are still consolidated into the report with their real status; the 5 failed ones are marked 'unknown' in the Surfaces audited table, never 'pass' or fabricated findings. No prompt pack generation is implied as a substitute for the missing verdict.
